Data audit

What the four Vizathon files contain, how they join, and what the pipeline must handle

Author

Michael Davies

Published

16 October 2026

The Chelsea FC Performance Insights Vizathon 2025 dataset contains simulated data for one player across four files. This audit records what each file holds, checks it against the data guide and against itself, and sets out the cleaning rules the pipeline will follow. Every number below is calculated from the data when this report renders.

4 files, all keyed by date

620 days where all three daily sources overlap

20 checks run: 5 pass, 11 notes, 4 issues

73% of capability rows are carried forward, not new tests

Summary

The data is clean in the ways that matter most for joining: every file has exactly one row per date (and per test or metric), dates parse without error, and missing values are recorded consistently. Three things need handling before analysis:

  1. Most capability rows are repeats. The file carries each result forward daily until the next test, so 73% of rows are copies. Trends and test counts must use only the 832 genuine results.
  2. GPS speed bands are not always nested. In 91 of 721 sessions, distance above a higher speed threshold exceeds distance above a lower one. Bands should be reported as given, never subtracted from each other.
  3. One priority-area status doesn’t match the data. The sprint target is marked “Achieved”, but the latest measured score sits just below the 65% threshold. A tracker built on this data should calculate status, not copy it.

Coverage

GPS covers three seasons; capability and recovery cover two. Analysis that combines sources should use the overlap window from 2 July 2023 to 12 March 2025. GPS has no data in June or July, so pre-season appears only in the recovery and capability files.

All checks

File Check Affected Status What it means
GPS One row per date None Pass Each date appears once, so date is a safe join key.
GPS Dates parse as day/month/year None Pass All dates valid.
GPS Days with no session recorded 141 of 862 Note Every calendar day has a row; days off are rows of zeros, not missing rows. Exclude them from averages.
GPS Match days with no data 3 of 147 Note All three fall in a 29-day block of zeros from 14 March 2025, which suggests a period of unavailability rather than errors.
GPS Speed bands are nested (>27 within >24 within >21 km/h) 91 of 721 Issue Higher-speed distance sometimes exceeds the band below it, which cannot happen if the bands are cumulative. Treat bands as approximate and avoid subtracting them to make zones.
GPS Acceleration bands are nested 3 of 721 Issue A handful of sessions have more efforts above 4.5 m/s² than above 3.5 m/s².
GPS Effort counts are whole numbers 721 of 721 Note Counts are fractional, a sign of simulation. Round for display only.
GPS Heart rate time fits within session duration 13 of 721 Note Time in HR zones exceeds session duration by more than 10% in a few sessions. HR may be recorded over a longer window.
GPS Continuous daily coverage in season 2 of 861 Note Daily from 1 August to 31 May each season; June and July are absent, so there is no GPS pre-season data.
Capability One row per date and test combination None Pass 20 movement, quality and expression combinations every day.
Capability Rows that are carried forward, not new results 9,007 of 12,400 Issue Values repeat until a new test, as the guide says. Use only new results for trends and test counts, or trends will look smoother and more frequent than they are.
Capability Missing benchmark scores 2,561 of 12,400 Note Missing where there is not yet enough data for a benchmark, mostly isometric tests early on.
Capability Scores outside 0–100% 389 of 9,839 Note Benchmark scores can exceed 100% or fall below 0, so they are relative scores rather than percentiles. Do not cap them.
Recovery One row per date and metric None Pass 13 metrics every day: 6 categories with 2 metrics each, plus the overall score.
Recovery Completeness of 0 always means no composite score None Pass Consistent: a composite exists only on days its tests were completed.
Recovery Days with an overall recovery score 371 of 621 Note The overall score exists on 60% of days. Missing means not collected, not zero.
Recovery Overall score equals the mean of the category composites 282 of 371 Note The overall score tracks the category mean but is not equal to it, so its weighting is unknown. Use it as supplied rather than recomputing it.
Priorities Review dates fall within the data 3 of 3 Note All three targets are reviewed on 7 May 2025, after the capability and recovery data end on 12 March 2025.
Priorities Targets can be measured from the data 2 of 3 Note Sleep is recorded as a relative quality score, not hours, and nutrition is not recorded at all. Only the sprint target maps to a measured score.
Priorities Sprint target status matches the data 1 of 1 Issue Marked “Achieved” (>65% max velocity score), but the latest dynamic max velocity score is 64.65% on 12 March 2025.

The files

GPS

862 rows, one per calendar day from 2 August 2022 to 11 April 2025, including 147 match days. Days without a session are stored as rows of zeros (141 days), so averages must exclude them. Match-day codes count up to 10 in both directions and stop there, so “10” means “10 or more”. Heart rate zones arrive as minutes and seconds; the reader converts them to minutes.

Physical capability

12,400 rows: 20 combinations of movement (agility, jump, sprint, upper body), quality and expression (isometric or dynamic), every day from 2 July 2023 to 12 March 2025. The score is a benchmark percentage that can exceed 100% or fall below 0. Across all combinations there are 832 genuine results on 252 test days.

Recovery status

8,073 rows in long format: 13 metrics a day from 2 July 2023 to 13 March 2025. Each of six categories has a completeness score (0 to 1) and a composite score relative to the player’s norm, plus one overall score. Missing means not collected; zero is a real zero. Infrequent tests such as blood markers will need carrying forward, with their age shown, if they are to sit on a daily view.

Individual priority areas

Priority Area Target Type Period Tracking Measurable here
1 Sleep Increase average sleep by 1hr per night Habit 7 Mar to 7 May 2025 On Track Partly: sleep is a quality score, not hours
2 Nutrition 45g of carbohydrate every half time Habit 7 Mar to 7 May 2025 On Track No: nutrition is not recorded
3 Sprint >65% in max velocity score Outcome 7 Mar to 7 May 2025 Achieved Yes: sprint max velocity benchmark

Three targets set on 7 March 2025 for review on 7 May 2025, after the other data ends. Only the sprint target can be checked against measured data.

How the files join

All four files describe one player, so date is the only join key. The GPS and recovery files have one row per day and join directly; capability joins on date once reduced to new results; priority areas apply to a date range rather than a single day.

From To Key Notes
GPS Recovery date 529 GPS days in the overlap, all with a recovery row
GPS Capability date = test_date Join to the most recent result on or before each date
Any Priority areas date between target_set and review_date Three targets, one shared period

Rules for the pipeline

  1. Read the GPS file as Latin-1, and parse all dates as day/month/year.
  2. Keep GPS rows of zeros as days without a session; exclude them from averages and load totals.
  3. Treat match-day code 10 as “10 or more” and derive match context from md_plus_code == 0.
  4. Report speed and acceleration bands as supplied; never subtract one band from another.
  5. Reduce capability data to new results before calculating trends, test frequency or change.
  6. Keep benchmark scores uncapped; they are relative scores, not percentiles.
  7. Treat missing recovery values as not collected; keep zeros as measured values.
  8. Use the overall recovery score as supplied rather than recomputing it.
  9. Restrict combined analyses to the overlap window, 2 July 2023 to 12 March 2025.
  10. Calculate priority-area status from the data where it can be measured, and show where it can’t.

Data: CFC Insights Vizathon 2025, Chelsea FC Performance Insights (simulated data for one player). Raw files are downloaded from the public competition repository, not stored here.
